claims.claim: Freight trains are on average three to four times more fuel efficient than trucks.
claims.episode_span: even when rail fuel efficiency is three to four times better per ton-mile
claims.source_title: Freight Rail & The Environment - Association of American Railroads
claims.supporting_quote: Trains are also three to four times more fuel efficient than trucks on average, with one train taking hundreds of trucks off the road.

claims.claim: A freight train can move one ton of freight nearly 500 miles on a single gallon of fuel, which puts the direct fuel-energy cost of rail well below one cent per ton-mile at typical diesel prices.
claims.episode_span: the direct energy cost for rail sits well below one cent per ton-mile at current commodity prices
claims.source_title: Freight Rail & The Environment - Association of American Railroads
claims.supporting_quote: On average, one train can move one ton of freight nearly 500 miles on a single gallon of fuel, making freight rail the most fuel-efficient way to move goods over land

claims.claim: The rolling resistance coefficient of a railroad steel wheel on steel rail is about 0.0010 to 0.0024 (passenger rail cars about 0.0020).
claims.episode_span: rolling resistance on steel is roughly 0.001 to 0.002 times the normal force
claims.supporting_quote: 0.0010 to 0.0024 [ 24 ] [ 25 ] 0.5 mm [ 3 ] Railroad steel wheel on steel rail. Passenger rail car about 0.0020

claims.claim: Driver wages averaged 81.8 cents per mile in 2025 against an industry-average total truck operating cost of $2.336 per mile (ATRI), i.e. roughly 35 percent of operating cost, consistent with the 30-40 percent range.
claims.episode_span: Driver wages currently represent 30 to 40 percent of many truck operating costs
claims.source_title: Truck Operating Costs Rose 3.4% in 2025, ATRI Finds - Transport Topics
claims.supporting_quote: Meanwhile, driver wages rose to 81.8 cents from 79.8 cents, an increase of 2.5%, and driver benefits climbed to 21 cents from 19.7 cents.

claims.claim: The US EIA rates diesel (ultra-low-sulfur distillate) at 137,381 Btu per gallon, about 145 MJ, consistent with the digest's 'roughly 140 megajoules per gallon'.
claims.episode_span: Diesel fuel contains roughly 140 megajoules per gallon
claims.source_title: Energy conversion calculators - U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
claims.supporting_quote: Diesel fuel and heating oil conversion calculator gallons Btu megajoules liters Clear Calculate 1 gallon= 137,381 Btu ( for distillate fuel with 15 ppm or less sulfur content at 5,770,000 Btu per barrel in 2026; estimate )

claims.claim: Typical rolling-resistance coefficients: 0.001-0.002 for railroad steel wheels on steel rails versus 0.006-0.01 for a truck tire on asphalt (a range overlapping the digest's 0.005-0.008).
claims.episode_span: rolling resistance on steel is roughly 0.001 to 0.002 times the normal force while truck tires run closer to 0.005 to 0.008
claims.supporting_quote: 0.005 dirty tram rails 0.006 - 0.01 truck tire on asphalt 0.008 bicycle tire on rough paved road

claims.claim: Trucks moved roughly 72.7% of US freight by weight in 2024 (American Trucking Associations).
claims.episode_span: Trucking grew dominant because it offers door-to-door service without transfers.
claims.source_title: Economics and Industry Data | American Trucking Associations
claims.supporting_quote: Trucks moved roughly 72.7% of the nation's freight by weight in 2024. That is just one of many statistics calculated and tracked by American Trucking Associations' economics department.

claims.claim: US freight railroads are privately owned and largely fund their own infrastructure, investing over $25 billion a year in their networks since 1980.
claims.episode_span: while railroads must maintain their own track and pay property taxes on it
claims.source_title: Freight Rail Overview - Association of American Railroads
claims.supporting_quote: Privately owned freight railroads invest billions in their own infrastructure, technology, and safety systems, supporting hundreds of thousands of skilled jobs and playing a critical role in U.S. commerce. Who funds freight railroads? Freight railroads largely fund themselves.

claims.claim: US rail freight moved 473 ton-miles per gallon of fuel in 2018, which at typical diesel prices puts the direct fuel cost well under one cent per ton-mile.
claims.episode_span: the direct energy cost for rail sits well below one cent per ton-mile at current commodity prices
claims.source_title: Rail transportation in the United States - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: In 2018, US rail freight had a transport energy efficiency of 473 ton-miles per gallon of fuel.
